bull_bear.body: This is the central topic of the call. Parent CET1 at 12.24% against 125% risk weights on gold leaves little headroom, and subsidiaries being carried at cost in the parent penalises the computation. The stated options, all held open simultaneously: QIP; secondary/partial stake sale in subsidiaries; strategic divestment or listing of the microfinance business; a demerger (which would itself release capital); and perpetual debt (Tier 1, up to 50% of equity) plus subordinated debt (Tier 2). Management is explicit about not wanting to dilute cheap: "we don't want to be in a desperate situation… we want to raise at some reasonable valuations." It also believes co-lending momentum plus perpetual/sub debt could carry it "for a quarter or 2 more."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Capital adequacy at the parent is the binding constraint.** Every growth conversation on this call routes back to it, and no option has been chosen.
- Gold price is explicitly named as a tail risk: "a sharp correction is a real tail risk in this environment." Management holds LTV discipline as the mitigant; LTV has nonetheless risen from 63% to 70%.
- 1–30 and 30–90 DPD buckets rose in gold, MSME (secured and unsecured). Management calls it seasonal and structural to the collection pattern (no penal charges before 90 days) and notes LGD in gold "has almost been 0" over 15–16 years — but the 30+ number is now 3.8%.
- Housing GNPA "much higher than the peers" — a two-year fix, not a quarter's.
- INR 475 cr income-tax demand under appeal at CIT; no new development.
- Management churn: CFO change (previous CFO on strategy, health reasons), unsecured-lending business head redeployed after the product was discontinued, Girish Kousgi newly onboard.
- An unresolved disclosure gap: standalone assignment volume rose from INR 4,200 cr to INR 4,800 cr YoY while assignment income fell from INR 173 cr to INR 43 cr; management could not explain it on the call and promised to revert.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Nirmal Jain is unusually plain-spoken about the weak spot — "our capital adequacy, which in the parent company is kind of at the edge, and we are like — we want to fix it." He is equally direct on AI: "AI is a new animal… This is not a tested technology," which is why the Project PACE benefit ranges (loss prevention 10–40%, operating cost 8–20%) are so wide. He conceded he could not reconcile the assignment-income question and committed to come back — a good sign. Girish Kousgi gave the only hard multi-year numbers on the call. Overall tone: confident on operations, deliberately non-committal on the capital route.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The off-book model is doing double duty — 96.7% core AUM plus INR 26,118 cr assigned and INR 14,647 cr co-lent is what keeps reported capital adequacy above threshold at all.
- Co-lending scaling is *dilutive to reported P&L* in the short run: it displaces upfront assignment gains, so standalone other income should keep falling even as the business improves.
- The new RBI gold framework is framed by management as a positive — it forces income assessment discipline and, in co-lending, banks must accept IIFL's underwriting process before starting, which is a moat once established across 15 partners.
- The credit-cost guidance is almost entirely a *housing* clean-up story (micro-LAP INR 440 cr + BLC INR 260 cr), not a gold or MFI story.

bull_bear.body:
- Consolidated CRAR (computed) at 23.5%, with standalone at 17%, IIFL Home Finance at 39%, and IIFL Samasta at 26%; net gearing at 4.1x consolidated.

- FY27 targets: ~25% AUM growth, 1.5-1.7% credit costs, 3.1-3.3% ROA, 16-20% ROE (equity raise will impact this), and 35-40% off-book loan assets.
- 3-year plan (FY28-FY30): ~20% AUM CAGR, 1.0-1.2% credit costs, 3.6-3.8% ROA, 18-20% ROE, and ~40% off-book loan assets.

business.body:
- **Gold (standalone):** the core. Portfolio yield rising as post-embargo low-yield loans run off and new small-ticket loans are booked at higher rates. New RBI framework implemented from April: income assessment now mandatory; consumption loans capped at 75% LTV, income-generating loans can exceed it with cash-flow assessment. IIFL has launched an income-generating gold loan product using Udyam certificates and business proof.
- **IIFL Home Finance:** micro-LAP outstanding INR 440 cr and BLC book INR 260 cr are the "problem book", to be cleaned up this year — this is what drives the elevated FY27 credit cost. Blended LGD on the housing book 33–34%. Onboarding yield up 68–70 bps over two quarters on incremental book, though *portfolio* yield is falling as the high-yield micro-LAP runs off. Pivoting to affordable and emerging; prime completely cut.
- **IIFL Samasta (microfinance):** recovered; 3–4% sequential growth expected to continue; diversifying into retail and secured products.
- **Discontinued:** unsecured business loans and personal loans both stopped. MSME unsecured is in run-off/recovery mode.

latest_quarter.body: Nirmal Jain does not see margin pressure in gold: IIFL focuses on small-ticket customers where "the rate at which we lend, given our scale, we afford", and portfolio yield is improving as older loans roll. In housing the opposite is happening — portfolio yield declines as high-yield (18–24%) micro-LAP runs off, even though incremental onboarding yield is up. Cost of funds rose slightly on the dollar bond (fully hedged) but is expected to fall as FCNR liquidity eases. The branch-led model with 4,500–5,000 branches is a heavy fixed-cost base, so scale gives disproportionate operating leverage — partly consumed by the 500 new branches planned this year.

outlook.body:
- **Credit cost:** 1.5% to 1.7% for FY27 (Slide 20), with a sharp decline over the following two years as the housing micro-LAP and BLC books are cleaned up.
- **Home finance (IIFL HFC):** book and AUM growth of 17–18% for full-year FY27; disbursement growth "over 30%". ROE target of mid-teens in about three years.
- **Microfinance (Samasta):** ROA to reach 2.5–3%, "closer to 3%", by end of the year; industry AUM growth ~3–4% per quarter.
- **ROA (consolidated):** improvement of 40–50 bps post-tax (60–70 bps pre-tax), of which 40–50 bps pre-tax from credit cost and 20–30 bps from operating cost and NIM.
- **Opex/AUM:** 3.3–3.4% range, with a downward trajectory over 2–3 years from AI plus operating leverage — offset partly by 500 new branches planned this year.
- **Margins:** expected to remain stable in gold despite competition; borrowing cost expected to ease as FCNR liquidity improves.
- **Security receipts:** SR book to be "completely wound up" more or less by September 2027; management expects realisation above book value.
- **Capital:** enabling resolution for fresh equity to be put to shareholders at the AGM two days after the call; valid for a full year.

outlook.body: Gold remains the primary engine but growth is being managed deliberately — 11% QoQ, of which 5–6% is tonnage growth, the rest value. LTV has moved from ~63% in March to ~70%. Co-lending is the key pipeline lever: it scaled slower than plan in Q1 but the company now has 15 active bank partners and expects momentum, which both eases capital pressure and reduces upfront assignment income (management guided that standalone assignment income "will become almost negligible in the next few quarters"). Home finance disbursements grew 39% sequentially, with home loans ~80% of the portfolio and LAP ~18–19%.

Management confirmed no new products are planned in the listed entity beyond LAP/secured MSME and a small loan-against-shares book. International funding diversification is a live vertical — the USD 500 mn social bond and an expected Fitch upgrade following Moody's.

outlook.body:
- Maintain highest standards of corporate governance with a well-informed, independent, and engaged Board providing strategic guidance and ensuring adherence to ethical business practices.
- Continually evaluate and adapt governance practices to remain aligned with the evolving business environment and markets.
- Leverage a diverse Board to retain competitive advantage through differences in thought, perspective, knowledge, skills, and experience.
- Ensure full alignment with the updated BRSR framework for ESG reporting and obtain assurance on BRSR Core disclosures.
- Dividend Distribution Policy considers business plan, capital requirements, free cash flow, debt-equity ratio, regulatory net worth, and adequacy of profits. Dividend may be expected when there is surplus in P&L or profits exceed 10% of equity capital; may not be expected when there are losses, profit is below 10% of equity, income/PAT declines more than 75% year-on-year, or business visibility is uncertain. Retained earnings are utilised for projected investments in business and subsidiaries, and to maintain regulatory capital adequacy.
- Financial Inclusion and Literacy: Constant endeavor to expand access to financial services to underserved people and groups such as small businesses or women, enabling market expansion and social impact-based borrowing.
- Community Development: Strong CSR practice in health, education, environment, livelihood, and poverty alleviation, designed to care for women and youth, make healthcare accessible to marginalized sections, and contribute to the fight against climate change.
- Digitalization: Leveraging digitalization to drive innovation across offerings and processes, including strategic fintech partnerships and in-house capabilities, to expand customer base and serve niche segments efficiently at lower cost.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Credit cost:** 1.5% to 1.7% for FY27 (Slide 20), with a sharp decline over the following two years as the housing micro-LAP and BLC books are cleaned up.
- **Home finance (IIFL HFC):** book and AUM growth of 17–18% for full-year FY27; disbursement growth "over 30%". ROE target of mid-teens in about three years.
- **Microfinance (Samasta):** ROA to reach 2.5–3%, "closer to 3%", by end of the year; industry AUM growth ~3–4% per quarter.
- **ROA (consolidated):** improvement of 40–50 bps post-tax (60–70 bps pre-tax), of which 40–50 bps pre-tax from credit cost and 20–30 bps from operating cost and NIM.
- **Opex/AUM:** 3.3–3.4% range, with a downward trajectory over 2–3 years from AI plus operating leverage — offset partly by 500 new branches planned this year.
- **Margins:** expected to remain stable in gold despite competition; borrowing cost expected to ease as FCNR liquidity improves.
- **Security receipts:** SR book to be "completely wound up" more or less by September 2027; management expects realisation above book value.
- **Capital:** enabling resolution for fresh equity to be put to shareholders at the AGM two days after the call; valid for a full year.
order book & pipeline: Gold remains the primary engine but growth is being managed deliberately — 11% QoQ, of which 5–6% is tonnage growth, the rest value. LTV has moved from ~63% in March to ~70%. Co-lending is the key pipeline lever: it scaled slower than plan in Q1 but the company now has 15 active bank partners and expects momentum, which both eases capital pressure and reduces upfront assignment income (management guided that standalone assignment income "will become almost negligible in the next few quarters"). Home finance disbursements grew 39% sequentially, with home loans ~80% of the portfolio and LAP ~18–19%.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Gold (standalone):** the core. Portfolio yield rising as post-embargo low-yield loans run off and new small-ticket loans are booked at higher rates. New RBI framework implemented from April: income assessment now mandatory; consumption loans capped at 75% LTV, income-generating loans can exceed it with cash-flow assessment. IIFL has launched an income-generating gold loan product using Udyam certificates and business proof.
- **IIFL Home Finance:** micro-LAP outstanding INR 440 cr and BLC book INR 260 cr are the "problem book", to be cleaned up this year — this is what drives the elevated FY27 credit cost. Blended LGD on the housing book 33–34%. Onboarding yield up 68–70 bps over two quarters on incremental book, though *portfolio* yield is falling as the high-yield micro-LAP runs off. Pivoting to affordable and emerging; prime completely cut.
- **IIFL Samasta (microfinance):** recovered; 3–4% sequential growth expected to continue; diversifying into retail and secured products.
- **Discontinued:** unsecured business loans and personal loans both stopped. MSME unsecured is in run-off/recovery mode.
growth verticals / optionality: Beyond the core, the optionality is structural rather than product-led: co-lending scaling with 15 bank partners, the off-book model releasing capital, and Project PACE (AI) moving "from pilot to measurable impact across collection, fraud detection, frontline productivity." Management confirmed no new products are planned in the listed entity beyond LAP/secured MSME and a small loan-against-shares book. International funding diversification is a live vertical — the USD 500 mn social bond and an expected Fitch upgrade following Moody's.
margins & cost dynamics: Nirmal Jain does not see margin pressure in gold: IIFL focuses on small-ticket customers where "the rate at which we lend, given our scale, we afford", and portfolio yield is improving as older loans roll. In housing the opposite is happening — portfolio yield declines as high-yield (18–24%) micro-LAP runs off, even though incremental onboarding yield is up. Cost of funds rose slightly on the dollar bond (fully hedged) but is expected to fall as FCNR liquidity eases. The branch-led model with 4,500–5,000 branches is a heavy fixed-cost base, so scale gives disproportionate operating leverage — partly consumed by the 500 new branches planned this year.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): The physical expansion commitment is 500 new branches in FY27, after adding none last year. This is explicitly flagged as a drag that will "mitigate the benefit of operating leverage."
capital allocation: This is the central topic of the call. Parent CET1 at 12.24% against 125% risk weights on gold leaves little headroom, and subsidiaries being carried at cost in the parent penalises the computation. The stated options, all held open simultaneously: QIP; secondary/partial stake sale in subsidiaries; strategic divestment or listing of the microfinance business; a demerger (which would itself release capital); and perpetual debt (Tier 1, up to 50% of equity) plus subordinated debt (Tier 2). Management is explicit about not wanting to dilute cheap: "we don't want to be in a desperate situation… we want to raise at some reasonable valuations." It also believes co-lending momentum plus perpetual/sub debt could carry it "for a quarter or 2 more."
risks & watch-items:
- **Capital adequacy at the parent is the binding constraint.** Every growth conversation on this call routes back to it, and no option has been chosen.
- Gold price is explicitly named as a tail risk: "a sharp correction is a real tail risk in this environment." Management holds LTV discipline as the mitigant; LTV has nonetheless risen from 63% to 70%.
- 1–30 and 30–90 DPD buckets rose in gold, MSME (secured and unsecured). Management calls it seasonal and structural to the collection pattern (no penal charges before 90 days) and notes LGD in gold "has almost been 0" over 15–16 years — but the 30+ number is now 3.8%.
- Housing GNPA "much higher than the peers" — a two-year fix, not a quarter's.
- INR 475 cr income-tax demand under appeal at CIT; no new development.
- Management churn: CFO change (previous CFO on strategy, health reasons), unsecured-lending business head redeployed after the product was discontinued, Girish Kousgi newly onboard.
- An unresolved disclosure gap: standalone assignment volume rose from INR 4,200 cr to INR 4,800 cr YoY while assignment income fell from INR 173 cr to INR 43 cr; management could not explain it on the call and promised to revert.
management quality / tone: Nirmal Jain is unusually plain-spoken about the weak spot — "our capital adequacy, which in the parent company is kind of at the edge, and we are like — we want to fix it." He is equally direct on AI: "AI is a new animal… This is not a tested technology," which is why the Project PACE benefit ranges (loss prevention 10–40%, operating cost 8–20%) are so wide. He conceded he could not reconcile the assignment-income question and committed to come back — a good sign. Girish Kousgi gave the only hard multi-year numbers on the call. Overall tone: confident on operations, deliberately non-committal on the capital route.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The off-book model is doing double duty — 96.7% core AUM plus INR 26,118 cr assigned and INR 14,647 cr co-lent is what keeps reported capital adequacy above threshold at all.
- Co-lending scaling is *dilutive to reported P&L* in the short run: it displaces upfront assignment gains, so standalone other income should keep falling even as the business improves.
- The new RBI gold framework is framed by management as a positive — it forces income assessment discipline and, in co-lending, banks must accept IIFL's underwriting process before starting, which is a moat once established across 15 partners.
- The credit-cost guidance is almost entirely a *housing* clean-up story (micro-LAP INR 440 cr + BLC INR 260 cr), not a gold or MFI story.

- **Q1 FY27 (this):** AUM crossed INR 1.15 lakh cr (+38% YoY); ROE 19.5%, ROA 3.1%; PAT INR 713 cr (+14% QoQ). GNPA 1.6%/NNPA 0.8%, both +9 bps QoQ. Gold AUM INR 58,406 cr, +11% QoQ (5–6% tonnage). LTV 63% → 70%. Board approved enabling resolution for fresh equity; parent CET1 12.24%. Moody's Ba3 assigned; USD 500 mn social bond raised. New RBI gold framework implemented; income-generating gold loan product launched. 500 new branches planned for FY27.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: which capital route was actually taken (QIP vs subsidiary stake sale vs microfinance listing vs perpetual debt) and at what valuation; whether HFC disbursement growth is tracking the >30% full-year path; credit cost against the 1.5–1.7% FY27 band; gold 30+ DPD after the "seasonal" explanation; co-lending AUM vs the 15-partner ramp; the promised follow-up on standalone assignment income._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Tokenised bonds] Completed a ₹25 Cr tokenised bond transaction, the first by a non-PSU NBFC in India, executed on MSEI under the SEBI Regulatory Sandbox framework, listed on India INX & NSE IX, with Sustainable Fitch as SPO provider.
- [GMTN bond issuance] Separately raised a US$300mn issue under its Global Medium Term Note programme (144A/Reg S), oversubscribed ~2.3x, with a 3.5-year tenor, alongside a Social Bonds tap issuance.
- [Group structure] IIFL Home Finance (since 2010/2016, formerly CDC Group backed, ~100% owned) and IIFL Samasta Finance (since 2011/2022, ~80% owned) are subsidiaries; promoter holding 24.8%, institutional investors 48.8% including Fairfax (13.6%), with public & others at 26.4% as of 30 Sep 2026.
- [Awards] Recognised as one of the 'ET Iconic Brands of India 2026' and among 'Top 50 India's Best Workplaces for Women 2026'; IIFL Foundation received the 'Best Innovation in CSR Practices Award' at the 17th CSR Summit.

one-line thesis: Profitability is "back to natural levels" — ROE 19.5%, ROA 3.1%, AUM up 38% YoY to INR 1.15 lakh crore on a book that is nearly 90% secured. The unresolved issue is capital: standalone CET1 is at 12.24% against 125% risk weights on gold, and the Board has taken an enabling resolution for fresh equity with QIP, subsidiary stake sale, microfinance listing/demerger and perpetual debt all held open. Management is candid that parent capital adequacy is "kind of at the edge."

| Core product AUM | INR 1,11,717 cr | +43% | +8% QoQ; now 96.7% of mix (home + gold + MSME + MFI) |
| PPOP | INR 1,252 cr | +50% | +7% QoQ |

| GNPA / NNPA | 1.6% / 0.8% | — | Both +9 bps QoQ; PCR on NPA 94% |

| ROE / ROA | 19.5% / 3.1% | — | Annualised |
| Cash / gearing | Cash + committed lines INR 7,148 cr | — | Net gearing 4.0x; positive ALM across all buckets |
> Off-book: assigned loan book INR 26,118 cr (+73% YoY, +10% QoQ); co-lending assets INR 14,647 cr (+27% YoY, +20% QoQ). Capital adequacy: NBFC 17.1%, HFC 41.7%, Samasta 24.9% (minimum ~15%). Raised INR 17,183 cr via term loans/bonds/CP plus INR 5,283 cr through direct assignment; USD 500 mn social bond. Moody's assigned Ba3 issuer rating (one notch above Fitch and S&P). Credit cost for Q1 ~1.6%. Opex/AUM down to 3.4%.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Credit cost:** 1.5% to 1.7% for FY27 (Slide 20), with a sharp decline over the following two years as the housing micro-LAP and BLC books are cleaned up.
- **Home finance (IIFL HFC):** book and AUM growth of 17–18% for full-year FY27; disbursement growth "over 30%". ROE target of mid-teens in about three years.
- **Microfinance (Samasta):** ROA to reach 2.5–3%, "closer to 3%", by end of the year; industry AUM growth ~3–4% per quarter.
- **ROA (consolidated):** improvement of 40–50 bps post-tax (60–70 bps pre-tax), of which 40–50 bps pre-tax from credit cost and 20–30 bps from operating cost and NIM.
- **Opex/AUM:** 3.3–3.4% range, with a downward trajectory over 2–3 years from AI plus operating leverage — offset partly by 500 new branches planned this year.
- **Margins:** expected to remain stable in gold despite competition; borrowing cost expected to ease as FCNR liquidity improves.
- **Security receipts:** SR book to be "completely wound up" more or less by September 2027; management expects realisation above book value.
- **Capital:** enabling resolution for fresh equity to be put to shareholders at the AGM two days after the call; valid for a full year.
order book & pipeline: Gold remains the primary engine but growth is being managed deliberately — 11% QoQ, of which 5–6% is tonnage growth, the rest value. LTV has moved from ~63% in March to ~70%. Co-lending is the key pipeline lever: it scaled slower than plan in Q1 but the company now has 15 active bank partners and expects momentum, which both eases capital pressure and reduces upfront assignment income (management guided that standalone assignment income "will become almost negligible in the next few quarters"). Home finance disbursements grew 39% sequentially, with home loans ~80% of the portfolio and LAP ~18–19%.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Gold (standalone):** the core. Portfolio yield rising as post-embargo low-yield loans run off and new small-ticket loans are booked at higher rates. New RBI framework implemented from April: income assessment now mandatory; consumption loans capped at 75% LTV, income-generating loans can exceed it with cash-flow assessment. IIFL has launched an income-generating gold loan product using Udyam certificates and business proof.
- **IIFL Home Finance:** micro-LAP outstanding INR 440 cr and BLC book INR 260 cr are the "problem book", to be cleaned up this year — this is what drives the elevated FY27 credit cost. Blended LGD on the housing book 33–34%. Onboarding yield up 68–70 bps over two quarters on incremental book, though *portfolio* yield is falling as the high-yield micro-LAP runs off. Pivoting to affordable and emerging; prime completely cut.
- **IIFL Samasta (microfinance):** recovered; 3–4% sequential growth expected to continue; diversifying into retail and secured products.
- **Discontinued:** unsecured business loans and personal loans both stopped. MSME unsecured is in run-off/recovery mode.
growth verticals / optionality: Beyond the core, the optionality is structural rather than product-led: co-lending scaling with 15 bank partners, the off-book model releasing capital, and Project PACE (AI) moving "from pilot to measurable impact across collection, fraud detection, frontline productivity." Management confirmed no new products are planned in the listed entity beyond LAP/secured MSME and a small loan-against-shares book. International funding diversification is a live vertical — the USD 500 mn social bond and an expected Fitch upgrade following Moody's.
margins & cost dynamics: Nirmal Jain does not see margin pressure in gold: IIFL focuses on small-ticket customers where "the rate at which we lend, given our scale, we afford", and portfolio yield is improving as older loans roll. In housing the opposite is happening — portfolio yield declines as high-yield (18–24%) micro-LAP runs off, even though incremental onboarding yield is up. Cost of funds rose slightly on the dollar bond (fully hedged) but is expected to fall as FCNR liquidity eases. The branch-led model with 4,500–5,000 branches is a heavy fixed-cost base, so scale gives disproportionate operating leverage — partly consumed by the 500 new branches planned this year.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): The physical expansion commitment is 500 new branches in FY27, after adding none last year. This is explicitly flagged as a drag that will "mitigate the benefit of operating leverage."
capital allocation: This is the central topic of the call. Parent CET1 at 12.24% against 125% risk weights on gold leaves little headroom, and subsidiaries being carried at cost in the parent penalises the computation. The stated options, all held open simultaneously: QIP; secondary/partial stake sale in subsidiaries; strategic divestment or listing of the microfinance business; a demerger (which would itself release capital); and perpetual debt (Tier 1, up to 50% of equity) plus subordinated debt (Tier 2). Management is explicit about not wanting to dilute cheap: "we don't want to be in a desperate situation… we want to raise at some reasonable valuations." It also believes co-lending momentum plus perpetual/sub debt could carry it "for a quarter or 2 more."
risks & watch-items:
- **Capital adequacy at the parent is the binding constraint.** Every growth conversation on this call routes back to it, and no option has been chosen.
- Gold price is explicitly named as a tail risk: "a sharp correction is a real tail risk in this environment." Management holds LTV discipline as the mitigant; LTV has nonetheless risen from 63% to 70%.
- 1–30 and 30–90 DPD buckets rose in gold, MSME (secured and unsecured). Management calls it seasonal and structural to the collection pattern (no penal charges before 90 days) and notes LGD in gold "has almost been 0" over 15–16 years — but the 30+ number is now 3.8%.
- Housing GNPA "much higher than the peers" — a two-year fix, not a quarter's.
- INR 475 cr income-tax demand under appeal at CIT; no new development.
- Management churn: CFO change (previous CFO on strategy, health reasons), unsecured-lending business head redeployed after the product was discontinued, Girish Kousgi newly onboard.
- An unresolved disclosure gap: standalone assignment volume rose from INR 4,200 cr to INR 4,800 cr YoY while assignment income fell from INR 173 cr to INR 43 cr; management could not explain it on the call and promised to revert.
management quality / tone: Nirmal Jain is unusually plain-spoken about the weak spot — "our capital adequacy, which in the parent company is kind of at the edge, and we are like — we want to fix it." He is equally direct on AI: "AI is a new animal… This is not a tested technology," which is why the Project PACE benefit ranges (loss prevention 10–40%, operating cost 8–20%) are so wide. He conceded he could not reconcile the assignment-income question and committed to come back — a good sign. Girish Kousgi gave the only hard multi-year numbers on the call. Overall tone: confident on operations, deliberately non-committal on the capital route.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The off-book model is doing double duty — 96.7% core AUM plus INR 26,118 cr assigned and INR 14,647 cr co-lent is what keeps reported capital adequacy above threshold at all.
- Co-lending scaling is *dilutive to reported P&L* in the short run: it displaces upfront assignment gains, so standalone other income should keep falling even as the business improves.
- The new RBI gold framework is framed by management as a positive — it forces income assessment discipline and, in co-lending, banks must accept IIFL's underwriting process before starting, which is a moat once established across 15 partners.
- The credit-cost guidance is almost entirely a *housing* clean-up story (micro-LAP INR 440 cr + BLC INR 260 cr), not a gold or MFI story.
